newsitem.title: USA: Saratoga County, N.Y., sees 4 pct tax rise - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saratoga County, N.Y., sees 4 pct tax rise - paper.

text.p: Saratoga County, New York, will increase its property tax rate by four percent if a preliminary $123.8 million budget is adopted, the Albany Times Union said on Thursday.

The tax increase is needed because of welfare reform, a smaller budget surplus, an unexpected drop in sales tax receipts and a stagnating property tax base, according to county officials quoted by the newspaper.
Overall, the county plans to spend $6.2 million less than earmarked in the previous budget, which called for more than $130 million in expenditures.
Saratoga County last raised property taxes in 1990, while the 1996 budget included a 10 percent tax cut, the newspaper said.
The Times Union quoted Supervisor Marvin LeRoy, a Republican, as saying, "Let's not forget 1996 brought a 10 percent tax cut. It's not going to be better anytime soon."
Saratoga County's proposed 1997 budget calls for an 11 cent rise in the tax rate to $2.77 per $1,000 of assessed value.
County officials told the newspaper that the additional $1.25 million that would be raised by the higher tax rate equals the increase in the county's social services costs.
However, the elimination of the 12-cent sewer tax could mean that some property owners would have their overall county tax rate drop by one cent.
The elimination of the sewer tax affects residents of Clifton Park, Halfmoon, Saratoga Springs, Wilton, Milton, Stillwater, Ballston and Saratoga.

Still, the paper noted that two nearby counties have proposed budgets with tax cuts. Albany County is planning a 0.5 percent cut and Renssalaer County has proposed a two percent drop. Schenectady County adopted a budget with no tax increase.
Saratoga County will hold a public hearing on the budget proposal on November 26 and plans to adopt the budget on December 11.
